groups.data: test data or test database technique

cards.subject: Jest
says: bundles its own assertions, mocking and coverage in one package
runs test files in parallel worker processes and is configured through a jest.config file
cards.use: want a batteries-included runner for a JavaScript project that is not built on Vite
not: needs a separate assertion library such as Chai before any test can run

cards.subject: Vitest
says: reuses the Vite configuration and transform pipeline for its tests
exposes a Jest-compatible API through the vi helper
cards.use: already build with Vite and want tests to share that configuration
not: can only run tests that were written for a browser

cards.subject: Mocha
says: provides test structure and a runner but leaves assertions and mocking to other libraries
is commonly paired with Chai for assertions and Sinon for spies
cards.use: want a minimal runner and prefer to pick your own assertion library
not: bundles its own mocking library

cards.subject: Node's built-in test runner
says: is started with node --test and needs no installed package
provides test, describe and it through the node:test module
cards.use: want tests for a small Node project without adding any dependency
not: requires Babel to run ES modules

cards.subject: pytest
says: discovers functions named test_* and checks them with plain assert statements
injects setup values into tests through fixtures named as arguments
cards.use: write Python tests and want readable asserts and reusable fixtures
not: requires every test to be a method on a class that inherits from TestCase

cards.subject: JUnit
says: is the standard unit testing framework for Java
marks test methods with the @Test annotation
cards.use: test a Java or Kotlin service on the JVM
not: is the main test framework for Python projects

cards.subject: PHPUnit
says: is the most widely used unit testing framework for PHP
has tests extend a TestCase class and call assertion methods on it
cards.use: test PHP application code with a conventional xUnit framework
not: runs tests written as JavaScript describe and it blocks

cards.subject: Go's testing package
says: runs functions named TestXxx when go test is invoked
ships in the standard library, so no third-party runner is needed
cards.use: write unit tests for a Go package
not: requires an external assertion library to compare any two values

cards.subject: Playwright
says: drives Chromium, Firefox and WebKit through one API
gives every test its own isolated browser context
records traces that can be replayed step by step
cards.use: need cross-browser end-to-end tests with built-in tracing
not: runs the test code inside the browser alongside the application

cards.subject: Cypress
says: runs the test code inside the browser alongside the application
retries queries and assertions automatically until they pass or time out
reruns tests in an interactive runner as files change
cards.use: want to watch and debug front-end tests live in the browser as you write them
not: controls the browser from a separate process over the WebDriver protocol

cards.subject: Selenium WebDriver
says: controls browsers through the W3C WebDriver protocol
has client bindings for Java, Python, C# and other languages
cards.use: already have a large end-to-end suite in a language such as Java
not: records traces and videos of every run by default

cards.subject: Puppeteer
says: is a Node library that automates a browser for screenshots, PDFs and scraping as well as testing
does not provide a test runner or assertion library of its own
cards.use: need to script a browser from Node for PDF generation or screenshots
not: comes with a built-in assertion and reporting system

cards.subject: Appium
says: automates native and hybrid mobile apps using the WebDriver protocol
drives iOS and Android devices or emulators from the same style of test script
cards.use: need automated tests of a native mobile app
not: can only test web pages in desktop browsers

cards.subject: A headless browser
says: runs without a visible window
is how browser tests normally run on a CI server
cards.use: run end-to-end tests on a machine with no display
not: cannot execute JavaScript

cards.subject: Auto-waiting
says: makes an action wait until the element is visible, enabled and stable before it acts
removes most of the need for fixed sleeps in browser tests
cards.use: see clicks fail because the element had not finished rendering
not: is turned on by adding a long timeout to every test

cards.subject: A web-first assertion
says: retries the check until the condition holds or the timeout expires
is written as await expect(locator).toBeVisible() rather than reading a boolean first
cards.use: need an assertion that tolerates a page that updates asynchronously
not: reads the value once and fails immediately if it is not yet true

cards.subject: A role-based locator
says: finds an element by its accessible role and name such as a button called Save
keeps tests aligned with what assistive technology exposes
cards.use: want selectors that survive CSS refactors and double as an accessibility check
not: is tied to the nesting of div elements on the page
like: A brittle CSS or XPath selector

cards.subject: A test id attribute
says: adds a data attribute such as data-testid used only to find the element
stays stable when visible text or styling changes
cards.use: have no accessible role or label that identifies the element uniquely
not: is read aloud by screen readers

cards.subject: A brittle CSS or XPath selector
says: is tied to page structure so it breaks when a wrapper element is added
is the usual reason a selector fails after an unrelated layout change
cards.use: hear that a test broke after a purely visual refactor
not: is the most resilient way to find an element

cards.subject: A page object
says: wraps a page's locators and actions in a class so tests read as intent
puts selector changes in one place instead of every test
cards.use: find the same ten selectors repeated across many end-to-end tests
not: hides assertions so that tests contain no expectations at all

cards.subject: Network interception
says: stubs or observes the HTTP requests the page makes, for example with page.route
lets a test force an error response without breaking the real backend
cards.use: need to test how the interface shows a failed API call
not: slows the browser to simulate a bad connection and nothing else

cards.subject: Stored authentication state
says: saves cookies and local storage after one login so later tests start already signed in
removes repeated UI logins from the run time of a large suite
cards.use: see hundreds of tests each spend seconds on the login screen
not: shares one live browser session between all parallel tests

cards.subject: A browser context
says: is an isolated profile with its own cookies, storage and session
is much cheaper to create than launching a new browser
cards.use: need two different users in one test without them sharing a session
not: is the same thing as a browser tab

cards.subject: A trace file
says: records actions, DOM snapshots, console output and network calls for a run
lets you debug a CI failure after the machine is gone
cards.use: need to understand why a test failed only on the CI server
not: is a plain text log with no page snapshots

cards.subject: React Testing Library
says: renders components into a DOM and queries them the way a user would
discourages asserting on internal state and implementation details
cards.use: test what a React component shows and does for the user
not: gives direct access to a component's state through a wrapper object

cards.subject: jsdom
says: implements the DOM in Node so component tests run without a real browser
does not perform layout, so element sizes and positions are meaningless
cards.use: run component tests quickly inside Node
not: renders pixels that can be compared against screenshots

cards.subject: happy-dom
says: emulates the browser DOM in Node with an emphasis on speed over completeness
is chosen as a lighter alternative when jsdom is too slow
cards.use: find the DOM environment is a bottleneck in a large component suite
not: runs the real browser engine under the hood

cards.subject: user-event
says: simulates a whole interaction such as typing with the events a browser would fire
is awaited because its methods are asynchronous
cards.use: want a click or keystroke to behave like a real user's
not: dispatches one raw DOM event and nothing else

cards.subject: fireEvent
says: dispatches a single DOM event directly without simulating the surrounding interaction
skips events such as focus and keydown that a real user would also trigger
cards.use: need to trigger one specific low-level event
not: types text one character at a time with realistic key events

cards.subject: A getBy query
says: throws immediately when no element or more than one element matches
suits asserting that an element is present right now
cards.use: expect an element to already be in the document
not: returns null when nothing matches

cards.subject: A queryBy query
says: returns null when nothing matches instead of throwing
suits asserting that an element is absent
cards.use: need to prove that a message is not displayed
not: waits for the element to appear

cards.subject: A findBy query
says: returns a promise that resolves once the element appears
fails after a timeout if the element never shows up
cards.use: expect an element to appear after a data fetch finishes
not: throws immediately if the element is missing at call time

cards.subject: waitFor
says: retries a callback until it stops throwing or a timeout passes
is used to assert on a result that appears after asynchronous work
cards.use: need a custom condition that no single query expresses
not: pauses the test for a fixed number of milliseconds

cards.subject: act
says: flushes pending React state updates and effects before assertions run
produces a warning when state changes happen outside it during a test
cards.use: see a warning that an update was not wrapped
not: makes asynchronous code synchronous permanently

cards.subject: jest-dom matchers
says: add assertions such as toBeInTheDocument and toBeDisabled for DOM nodes
make failures read in terms of the page rather than raw properties
cards.use: want readable assertions about DOM state
not: replace the need for any query function

cards.subject: supertest
says: sends HTTP requests to a Node server in process and asserts on the response
binds the app to an ephemeral port, so no server needs to be started separately
cards.use: want to test Express routes without deploying or listening on a fixed port
not: drives a real browser to click through pages

cards.subject: A framework test client
says: calls the application's routes without opening a network socket
is provided by frameworks such as Django and Laravel for request-level tests
cards.use: want request tests that skip the web server entirely
not: requires the app to be deployed to a staging host

cards.subject: A black-box API test
says: calls a deployed environment over the real network
exercises routing, TLS and infrastructure that in-process tests skip
cards.use: need to confirm a deployed service answers correctly after a release
not: inspects the application's internal functions directly

cards.subject: Pact
says: records what a consumer expects from a provider as a contract file
lets the provider verify that contract in its own pipeline
cards.use: want a provider team to learn before deploying that a change breaks a consumer
not: load tests an API with many virtual users

cards.subject: Response schema validation
says: checks that real responses conform to the documented schema such as an OpenAPI definition
catches a field that was renamed or changed type
cards.use: suspect the implementation has drifted from the published API description
not: verifies that the provider meets each consumer's specific expectations

cards.subject: Newman
says: runs a Postman collection from the command line
lets a collection created in a GUI run as a CI step
cards.use: need to run an existing Postman collection in a pipeline
not: compiles Postman scripts into a native binary for load tests

cards.subject: REST Assured
says: is a Java library with a given-when-then DSL for testing REST services
lets a JVM team assert on status, headers and JSON paths fluently
cards.use: test a REST service from Java code with readable assertions
not: is a Node library that binds an Express app to a port

cards.subject: A negative API test
says: sends malformed, unauthorised or forbidden requests and expects a 4xx response
proves the endpoint rejects what it should reject
cards.use: want proof that a protected route refuses a caller with no token
not: only repeats the happy-path request with different data

cards.subject: An OpenAPI mock server
says: answers requests with example responses generated from the specification
lets front-end work start before the backend exists
cards.use: need a stand-in API while the real one is not built
not: records live traffic and replays it later

cards.subject: A mock function
says: records its calls, arguments and return values
can be given a return value or implementation per test, for example with vi.fn or jest.fn
cards.use: need to assert that a callback was called with specific arguments
not: replaces a whole imported module

cards.subject: A spy on a method
says: wraps an existing method so calls are recorded while the original can still run
can be put back with mockRestore
cards.use: want to watch a real method without replacing it permanently
not: replaces every export of a module at import time

cards.subject: A module mock
says: replaces an imported module for the whole test file, for example with vi.mock or jest.mock
is hoisted above the import statements
cards.use: need every import of a dependency to be replaced for a file
not: only affects one call of one function

cards.subject: A manual mock in __mocks__
says: lives in a __mocks__ folder next to the module it replaces
is picked up when the module mock is requested for that path
cards.use: want one reusable stand-in for a module shared by many tests
not: is generated automatically by the runner from the real code

cards.subject: Sinon
says: is a standalone library of spies, stubs and fake timers that works with any runner
provides a sandbox that restores everything in one call
cards.use: use Mocha and need test doubles from a separate library
not: is the mocking system built into Jest

cards.subject: Mock Service Worker
says: intercepts requests at the network layer so application code stays unchanged
uses the same request handlers in the browser and in Node
cards.use: want API mocks that work for both tests and local development
not: patches the fetch function inside each component

cards.subject: nock
says: intercepts outgoing HTTP calls in Node and replies with canned responses
can fail a test that makes an unexpected request when networking is disabled
cards.use: test Node code that calls a third-party HTTP API
not: intercepts requests in a browser service worker

cards.subject: Fake timers
says: replace setTimeout and Date so the test moves time forward by hand
make a one-second timeout testable without waiting
cards.use: need to test a debounce or a retry delay quickly
not: slow the real clock down

cards.subject: mockClear
says: resets recorded calls and results while keeping the configured implementation
is what stops one test's call counts leaking into the next
cards.use: see call counts from an earlier test affecting assertions
not: restores the original implementation of a spied method

cards.subject: Dependency injection for tests
says: passes collaborators in as parameters so a test can supply fakes without patching modules
reduces the need for module-level mocking
cards.use: find tests that need heavy module mocking just to replace one client
not: requires a mocking framework to function

cards.subject: Over-mocking
says: produces tests that mirror the implementation and pass while the real integration is broken
hides defects in SQL, serialisation and wiring
cards.use: see unit tests pass while a production bug in a database query ships
not: makes tests slower than using real dependencies

cards.subject: toMatchSnapshot
says: stores serialised output in a .snap file on the first run and compares against it later
produces a stored file that is reviewed in a pull request like code
cards.use: want to detect any unexpected change to a large rendered output
not: writes the expected value into the test source file

cards.subject: toMatchInlineSnapshot
says: writes the expected value into the test source itself
keeps the expectation next to the assertion for a short output
cards.use: want a small snapshot visible in the test without opening another file
not: stores the output in a separate .snap file

cards.subject: The snapshot update flag
says: rewrites stored snapshots with the current output when passed to the runner
should be used only after reading the diff
cards.use: have intentionally changed output and need to accept the new snapshot
not: deletes tests whose snapshots fail

cards.subject: An obsolete snapshot
says: is a stored snapshot that no test uses any more
is reported by the runner and can be removed with the update flag
cards.use: see a report of snapshots left over from a deleted test
not: is a snapshot that fails because output changed

cards.subject: A snapshot property matcher
says: lets non-deterministic fields such as ids and dates match by type
keeps generated values from failing the snapshot on every run
cards.use: see a snapshot fail only because a timestamp changed
not: freezes the system clock for the whole suite

cards.subject: A snapshot serializer
says: controls how a value is converted to text before it is stored
can hide noise or format custom objects readably
cards.use: need class instances or generated names to appear stably in snapshots
not: compares two snapshot files line by line

cards.subject: A giant snapshot
says: is approved without being read, so it stops catching defects
fails for so many unrelated reasons that people update it blindly
cards.use: hear that a team updates snapshots without reviewing them
not: is the best way to check precise behaviour of one function

cards.subject: A screenshot assertion
says: compares a rendered page with a stored baseline image and fails above a pixel tolerance
is available in Playwright as toHaveScreenshot
cards.use: want to catch an unintended visual change that DOM checks miss
not: compares the serialised DOM tree to a .snap file

cards.subject: Storybook
says: renders components in isolation as stories
gives visual and accessibility tools a stable set of states to test
cards.use: want each component state available to visual regression tools
not: is a replacement for the unit test runner

cards.subject: BackstopJS
says: runs screenshot comparisons driven by a scenario configuration file
produces a report that shows reference, test and difference images
cards.use: want a standalone visual regression tool configured by scenarios
not: renders components from stories in isolation

cards.subject: Masking dynamic regions
says: hides areas such as dates, ads and avatars before a screenshot is compared
cuts false alarms in visual tests
cards.use: see visual diffs fail every run because of a rotating banner
not: raises the allowed pixel difference for the entire page

cards.subject: A baseline screenshot
says: is the approved image a later capture is compared with
should be generated in the same environment that will run the comparison
cards.use: see visual tests pass locally and fail in CI because of font rendering
not: is regenerated automatically on every run

cards.subject: Istanbul
says: instruments source code to count executed statements, branches and functions
is the instrumentation behind the nyc command-line tool
cards.use: need coverage from code instrumented before it runs
not: reads coverage data that the JavaScript engine collects natively

cards.subject: V8 coverage
says: collects coverage natively from the JavaScript engine without rewriting the code
is available through the coverage provider setting in modern runners
cards.use: want coverage with less overhead and no instrumentation step
not: adds counters to the source before it runs

cards.subject: An lcov report
says: is a text format read by IDE plugins and coverage services
lists hit counts per line, function and branch for each file
cards.use: need to upload coverage to an external reporting service
not: is a human-friendly HTML page with colours

cards.subject: An HTML coverage report
says: highlights covered and uncovered lines in each source file
is opened in a browser to find what a test run missed
cards.use: want to see exactly which branches no test touched
not: is the format coverage services ingest

cards.subject: A coverage threshold
says: fails the run when a percentage falls below a configured value
turns coverage from a report into a gate
cards.use: want a pull request blocked if coverage drops below the agreed level
not: adds tests automatically until the number is reached

cards.subject: Diff coverage
says: measures coverage only on the lines changed in a pull request
stops a good overall number from hiding untested new code
cards.use: find new code is untested while the project total stays high
not: counts every file in the repository equally

cards.subject: Coverage include patterns
says: decide which source files are counted, including files no test imports
stop untested files from being left out of the percentage
cards.use: see a high coverage number while many source files are never imported
not: exclude generated files from the test run

cards.subject: Stryker
says: is a mutation testing framework for JavaScript and TypeScript
changes operators in the code and checks whether any test fails
cards.use: want to know whether tests would notice a changed condition
not: measures which lines a test executes

cards.subject: PIT
says: is a mutation testing system for Java
reports mutants that survived because no test failed
cards.use: want mutation scores for a JVM codebase
not: is a JavaScript coverage instrumenter

cards.subject: Watch mode
says: reruns tests related to changed files whenever you save
gives fast feedback while developing
cards.use: want the relevant tests to rerun on every save
not: runs the whole suite once and exits with a status code

cards.subject: Filtering tests by name
says: runs only the tests whose names match a pattern, for example with -t
is useful when debugging one failing case
cards.use: need to run one failing test without the rest of the suite
not: skips tests whose names match a pattern permanently

cards.subject: A focused test
says: is marked with only so the runner executes it and skips the others in the file
must never be committed because it silently disables the rest
cards.use: find a suite that passes in CI but runs one test
not: is reported as a to-do and never run

cards.subject: Parallel workers
says: run test files in separate processes or threads
speed up a suite but expose shared-state problems
cards.use: see a suite get faster but start failing intermittently
not: run the tests inside one file strictly in sequence

cards.subject: Test sharding
says: splits the test files across several machines or jobs
is selected with a flag such as --shard=2/4
cards.use: need to cut CI time by spreading the suite over runners
not: runs files in several threads on one machine

cards.subject: A setup file
says: runs before each test file to register matchers or global mocks
keeps shared test configuration out of individual tests
cards.use: want custom matchers available in every test file
not: runs once before the whole run starts

cards.subject: A global setup
says: runs once before the entire test run, for example to start a database
can export a teardown that runs after the last test
cards.use: need one expensive resource started once for the full suite
not: runs again before every test file

cards.subject: A test timeout
says: fails a test that takes longer than the configured limit
prevents a hung promise from stalling the run forever
cards.use: see a test hang waiting for a promise that never resolves
not: pauses a test until a condition becomes true

cards.subject: A reporter
says: formats results as dots, a tree, JUnit XML or JSON
is how CI systems read test results
cards.use: need results in a format a CI dashboard can parse
not: decides which tests run

cards.subject: A retry on failure setting
says: reruns a failing test and can mark it flaky if a retry passes
hides instability unless the passed-on-retry tests are reported
cards.use: see failures vanish after being rerun
not: fixes the root cause of a race condition

cards.subject: Bail
says: stops the run after a set number of failures
saves minutes when early failures make the rest meaningless
cards.use: want a broken build to stop quickly
not: reruns failed tests until they pass

cards.subject: Multi-project configuration
says: runs groups of tests with different environments or settings in one invocation
lets node and jsdom tests use separate configs together
cards.use: have server tests needing node and component tests needing a DOM
not: splits one test file across several machines

cards.subject: A pytest fixture
says: is a function marked with @pytest.fixture that a test requests by naming it as an argument
can be scoped to a function, module or session
cards.use: need a database connection created once and shared by many Python tests
not: must be called manually at the top of each test

cards.subject: A Playwright fixture
says: extends the test function with a setup value that is created only for tests that ask for it
tears itself down after the test that used it
cards.use: need a logged-in page object available only to tests that request it
not: runs before every test whether it is used or not

cards.subject: A beforeEach hook
says: runs setup code before every test in its scope
gives each test fresh state instead of sharing objects between tests
cards.use: want each test to start with a new instance of the object under test
not: runs once before the first test of the run

cards.subject: A factory function
says: generates valid objects with sensible defaults that a test overrides
makes a test show only the fields that matter to it
cards.use: find every test hand-writing a long user object
not: generates random values with no way to control them

cards.subject: Faker
says: generates realistic fake names, emails and addresses
accepts a seed so a failing run can be reproduced exactly
cards.use: need plentiful realistic-looking data for tests
not: returns the same value for the same field in every run, with no seed

cards.subject: Testcontainers
says: starts disposable real services such as databases in containers from test code
lets integration tests use the same engine as production
cards.use: want integration tests against real Postgres without a shared test server
not: replaces the database with an in-process fake

cards.subject: An in-memory test database
says: avoids disk and server setup, so suites start quickly
can differ from the production SQL dialect and hide dialect-specific bugs
cards.use: want very fast database tests and accept some dialect risk
not: is guaranteed to behave exactly like the production engine

cards.subject: PGlite
says: runs Postgres compiled to WebAssembly inside the test process
gives the real Postgres dialect without a server or container
cards.use: want Postgres behaviour in tests with no Docker
not: is a SQLite build with a Postgres-like syntax

cards.subject: A database per worker
says: gives each parallel test process its own database or schema
stops parallel files from overwriting each other's rows
cards.use: see intermittent failures only when tests run in parallel against one database
not: serialises all tests into a single process
like: Real migrations in the test database

cards.subject: Real migrations in the test database
says: build the test schema from the same migration files used in production
catch a broken migration before it reaches a real database
cards.use: find tests passing against a hand-written schema that does not match production
not: populate tables with seed rows

cards.subject: Truncating tables between tests
says: empties tables with a single statement, so cleanup works across connections
is slower than rolling back a transaction but needs no shared connection
cards.use: need cleanup for code that opens its own database connections
not: undoes a test's changes by rolling back one transaction
like: Real migrations in the test database

cards.subject: axe-core
says: is an open-source engine that runs accessibility rules against a page or DOM
reports violations with an impact level and the elements affected
cards.use: want an automated accessibility rule engine to embed in tests
not: is a browser automation tool

cards.subject: jest-axe
says: adds a toHaveNoViolations matcher that runs axe on rendered HTML
is used in Jest-style component tests
cards.use: want component tests to fail on accessibility violations
not: runs axe in a full browser against a deployed page

cards.subject: AxeBuilder
says: is the Playwright integration that runs axe against a live page
can scope the scan with include, exclude and tag options
cards.use: want an accessibility scan inside a Playwright end-to-end test
not: is a matcher added to Jest's expect

cards.subject: Lighthouse
says: audits a page for performance, accessibility and other categories
scores the accessibility category using a subset of automated checks
cards.use: want one report covering performance and accessibility
not: only audits accessibility

cards.subject: pa11y
says: runs accessibility checks on URLs from the command line or CI
can be scheduled across a list of pages
cards.use: want a simple command-line accessibility check across several URLs
not: is a unit test matcher for components

cards.subject: eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y
says: lints JSX for accessibility mistakes such as images without alt text
catches problems at edit time before any test runs
cards.use: want accessibility mistakes flagged in the editor and in lint
not: scans a rendered page in a browser

cards.subject: An axe WCAG tag filter
says: limits a scan to rules tagged for a given WCAG level, for example wcag2a
lets a team track conformance against one target
cards.use: need a scan that reports only rules for a chosen conformance level
not: disables axe for pages that have already been checked

cards.subject: A manual screen reader pass
says: finds problems automated rules cannot judge, such as whether alt text is meaningful
complements axe rather than being replaced by it
cards.use: hear that the site is accessible because axe reported no violations
not: is unnecessary once an automated scan passes

cards.subject: k6
says: has test scripts written in JavaScript and run by a Go-based engine
ships as a single binary and provides a built-in http module for scripts
cards.use: want load tests as code with pass-or-fail criteria
not: builds test plans in a graphical editor saved as XML

cards.subject: JMeter
says: builds test plans in a graphical editor and saves them as .jmx files
should run in non-GUI mode for real load generation
cards.use: inherit a load test saved as a graphical test plan
not: describes scenarios as JavaScript functions

cards.subject: Gatling
says: describes scenarios as code in a DSL on an asynchronous, non-blocking engine
produces an HTML report after each simulation
cards.use: want code-based scenarios on the JVM with detailed reports
not: configures load only through a graphical editor

cards.subject: Locust
says: defines user behaviour as Python classes with @task methods
can spread load over several worker machines
cards.use: want to write load scenarios in Python
not: uses an XML test plan

cards.subject: A virtual user
says: is a simulated client that runs the scenario script in a loop
lets one machine represent many concurrent users
cards.use: need to simulate many concurrent visitors from one load generator
not: is a person recruited to test manually

cards.subject: Think time
says: is the pause a script inserts between actions to mimic a person reading the page
makes the generated load more realistic
cards.use: see load numbers far above what real users produce
not: is the time the server takes to respond

cards.subject: A ramping stage
says: raises the number of virtual users gradually over a period
avoids a sudden spike that hides when degradation began
cards.use: want to find the load at which latency starts to climb
not: holds a fixed user count for the whole test

cards.subject: A pass-or-fail threshold
says: turns a metric such as p95 latency into a criterion that fails the run
makes load tests usable as a CI gate
cards.use: want a performance regression to fail the pipeline
not: decides how many virtual users start

cards.subject: An open workload model
says: starts new requests at a fixed arrival rate regardless of response time
keeps sending when the system slows down, like real independent users
cards.use: model public traffic where users arrive independently
not: waits for each response before sending the next

cards.subject: A closed workload model
says: keeps a fixed number of users, each waiting for its response before the next request
slows its own request rate when the system gets slow
cards.use: model a fixed pool of users such as staff on an internal system
not: sends at a constant arrival rate no matter what

cards.subject: Coordinated omission
says: understates latency because a stalled system makes the tool send fewer requests
is avoided by measuring from the intended send time
cards.use: hear low reported latency from a tool that waits for each response
not: means that two virtual users sent the same request

cards.subject: Dependency caching
says: restores installed packages between pipeline runs keyed on the lockfile
cuts installation time without changing results
cards.use: see most of the pipeline time spent downloading packages
not: skips running the tests whose files did not change

cards.subject: A service container
says: starts a real database or queue next to the job for integration tests
is removed when the job ends
cards.use: need a real Mongo or Postgres available to CI integration tests
not: mocks the database inside the test code

cards.subject: A matrix build
says: runs the same job across combinations such as Node versions or operating systems
reveals environment-specific failures
cards.use: need to confirm the code works on several runtime versions
not: splits one suite into slices

cards.subject: A JUnit XML report
says: is a standard result file CI dashboards parse to list failed tests
is written by a reporter option in most runners
cards.use: want failed tests listed in the CI interface instead of raw logs
not: is a coverage format

cards.subject: A failure artifact
says: uploads traces, screenshots and videos when a job fails
preserves evidence that disappears when the runner is destroyed
cards.use: cannot reproduce a failure that happened only in CI
not: caches dependencies between runs

cards.subject: The CI environment flag
says: makes tools such as Vitest run once instead of entering watch mode
is the CI variable most runners check for
cards.use: find a pipeline hanging because the runner waits for file changes
not: makes every test pass faster

cards.subject: The Jest --ci option
says: stops new snapshots being written automatically
makes a missing snapshot fail instead of being created
cards.use: want a CI run to fail when a snapshot file is absent
not: updates all stale snapshots

cards.subject: Browser binaries in CI
says: must be installed or come from a prepared image before end-to-end tests run
are best pinned so local and CI results match
cards.use: see end-to-end jobs fail because no browser is installed
not: are bundled with the test runner package itself

cards.subject: Merging shard coverage
says: combines partial coverage reports from parallel jobs into one total
is needed before a threshold can be applied across shards
cards.use: see each sharded job reporting only a slice of the coverage
not: splits the report into one file per source directory

cards.subject: Tests against a preview deployment
says: run end-to-end checks on a per-pull-request deployment
find problems that a local build cannot
cards.use: want browser tests to hit a temporary environment for the change
not: run the full suite on the production site

cards.subject: A forbid-only setting
says: fails the run if a focused test is present
prevents a committed only from silently skipping the suite
cards.use: want CI to reject a committed only
not: marks planned tests as to-do

cards.subject: makeTestDb in ggsocial
says: creates an in-memory Postgres with PGlite
builds the real app schema inside it using drizzle-kit's pushSchema
cards.use: read how ggsocial tests avoid needing a live Postgres
not: starts a Docker container with a full Postgres server

cards.subject: ggsocial's database mock
says: replaces the app's database module with vi.mock("@/lib/db")
lets each test seed its own brands, users and memberships
cards.use: read how ggsocial tests point application code at the test database
not: connects to the shared staging database

cards.subject: ggsocial's server-only alias
says: points the server-only package at a stub in the Vitest config
exists because that package deliberately throws outside a real Next.js server build
cards.use: see a ggsocial test fail on importing a server-only module
not: turns the node test environment into a browser one

cards.subject: GGMONEY_TEST_DRIVER
says: switches ggmoney's suite from SQLite to MySQL when set to mysql
proves the two database schemas behave identically
cards.use: want ggmoney tests to prove behaviour under MySQL strict mode
not: sets which tax year the tests treat as verified

cards.subject: TAX_YEARS_VERIFIED
says: is defined in ggmoney's tests so unverified tax years are not presented as checked
keeps payroll warning until a tax year is verified
cards.use: read how ggmoney avoids presenting unchecked tax figures as correct
not: selects the database driver for the test run

cards.subject: Moksy's itest suites
says: are *.itest.mjs files that persist through real Mongoose models against a real Mongo
need a Mongo service container in CI
cards.use: read how Moksy proves unique indexes and guarded updates
not: use an in-memory SQLite database

cards.subject: Moksy's dashboard e2e script
says: runs a Vitest flow test rather than a real browser
covers the requirements-to-document flow
cards.use: hear that the Moksy dashboard has an e2e script and ask whether it uses a browser
not: launches Playwright against the deployed dashboard

cards.subject: Moksy's Playwright dependency
says: appears only as a declared dependency in foundation/requirements/package.json
has no playwright.config anywhere in the repos
cards.use: hear a claim that Moksy has established browser end-to-end tests
not: drives the dashboard's end-to-end script

cards.subject: Moksy's node --test packages
says: run on Node's built-in test runner rather than Vitest
coexist with many services that carry a vitest.config.js
cards.use: find some Moksy packages with no Vitest config
not: are run by Jest

cards.subject: GGLearn's check:dynamic
says: self-tests dynamic question families by executing real node, python, php, sqlite3, git, semver and tsc
checks that each stated answer matches what real execution produces
cards.use: want to know whether generated question answers are correct
not: unit tests the login and scoring logic

cards.subject: GG repositories and Jest
says: do not use Jest, since no repository has a Jest config
use Vitest in ggsocial and plain PHP scripts in ggmoney
cards.use: are asked whether Jest is used in any GG repository
not: use Jest in ggsocial

qa.q: What does this line check in Jest or Vitest?
qa.right: It asserts that sum(2, 3) returns exactly 5
wrong: It runs sum five times and counts the calls
It replaces sum with a mock that returns 5
It waits five milliseconds for sum to finish
qa.why: toBe is a strict-equality matcher, so the assertion passes only when the value is 5.

qa.q: Why does this assertion fail even though both objects look the same?
qa.right: toBe compares by identity and two separate literals are different objects
wrong: Objects can never be compared in a test
The property a is a number, so a number-only matcher is required
The matcher must be awaited before it compares anything
qa.why: toBe uses Object.is. Use toEqual to compare structure.

qa.q: What is wrong with this test?
qa.right: The promise is not returned or awaited, so the test can finish before the assertion runs
wrong: resolves is not a valid matcher
toEqual cannot compare objects containing ids
fetchUser must always be replaced with a mock
qa.why: Without return or await, a rejected assertion can be reported after the test has already passed.

qa.q: In Vitest, which call creates a mock function?
qa.right: vi.fn()
wrong: jest.fn(), which works unchanged in Vitest
mock.create()
test.spy()
qa.why: Vitest exposes its mocking helpers on vi, not on jest.

qa.q: Which command runs this file with Node's built-in test runner?
qa.right: node --test
wrong: node --jest
npm install node-test
node run-tests
qa.why: The node:test module is executed by the node --test command and needs no installed package.

qa.q: Why use queryByText here rather than getByText?
qa.right: getByText would throw when nothing matches, while queryByText returns null so absence can be asserted
wrong: queryByText waits for the element to appear
getByText cannot find text inside buttons
queryByText ignores hidden elements only
qa.why: queryBy queries return null on no match, which is what an absence assertion needs.

qa.q: What does findByText do that getByText does not?
qa.right: It waits and retries until the text appears or a timeout passes
wrong: It matches text case-insensitively by default
It returns every matching element in an array
It ignores elements that are not visible
qa.why: findBy queries return a promise, so they suit content that appears after asynchronous work.

qa.q: Why is the textbox found by role and name?
qa.right: It locates the input the way a user or assistive technology would, by role and accessible name
wrong: It is the only query that works in jsdom
It matches the CSS class called email
It is always faster than any other query
qa.why: Role queries reward accessible markup and are less coupled to implementation.
qa.code:
const user = userEvent.setup();
await user.type(screen.getByRole("textbox", { name: /email/i }), "a@b.co");

qa.q: What is the problem with this React Testing Library assertion?
qa.right: It checks internal component state instead of what the user sees
wrong: It runs before the component renders
It uses a matcher that does not exist
It requires act to be removed
qa.why: Testing Library encourages asserting on rendered output, so refactors do not break tests.

qa.q: What does request(app) do in this supertest call?
qa.right: It sends the request to the app in process on an ephemeral port, with no server started by you
wrong: It requires the app to be listening on port 3000 first
It replaces the app with a mock
It opens the route in a browser
qa.why: supertest binds the app to a temporary port for the request.
qa.code:
const res = await request(app).post("/login").send({ email, password });
expect(res.status).toBe(401);

qa.q: After adding supertest tests, Jest prints that it did not exit one second after the run. app.js calls app.listen when imported. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Export the app without listening and call listen only in a separate server entry file
wrong: Raise the Jest timeout to 60 seconds
Call process.exit at the end of every test
Run the tests with a different assertion library
qa.why: Importing a module that opens a port leaves a handle open. Separating app from server fixes it.

qa.q: Why is the second form better in a Playwright test?
qa.right: The web-first assertion retries until visible or the timeout expires, while isVisible is read once
wrong: isVisible throws on hidden elements
The first form does not support text locators
The retrying form runs synchronously
qa.why: await expect(locator).toBeVisible() is retried, so it tolerates asynchronous rendering.

qa.q: What is the main problem with this line in an end-to-end test?
qa.right: A fixed sleep wastes time when the app is fast and still flakes when it is slow
wrong: waitForTimeout is not available in browsers
It cancels all pending network requests
It blocks other tests from starting
qa.why: Wait for a condition such as an element or response, not a fixed duration.

qa.q: What is this route handler used for?
qa.right: Making the orders request fail so the error state of the page can be tested
wrong: Slowing the page to measure performance
Recording the real response for later playback
Blocking the page from loading images
qa.why: page.route intercepts matching requests and can fulfil them with a controlled response.

qa.q: A suite of 200 Playwright tests each log in through the UI and takes too long. What should the team do first?
qa.right: Log in once in a setup step, save the storage state and reuse it in the tests
wrong: Disable parallel workers so the logins do not clash
Replace the tests with snapshot tests
Increase the test timeout for every test
qa.why: Stored authentication state removes the repeated login from each test's run time.

qa.q: Why can't you write const el = await cy.get(".price") in Cypress?
qa.right: Cypress commands are queued and chainable, not promises
wrong: cy.get returns a string
await is forbidden in all JavaScript tests
cy.get only works inside beforeEach
qa.why: Cypress enqueues commands and runs them in order, so you chain .then instead of awaiting.

qa.q: Why does the mock apply even though vi.mock is written after the import?
qa.right: vi.mock is hoisted above the imports before the module graph loads
wrong: Imports are evaluated lazily at the end of the file
The runner re-imports the file after each assertion
vi.mock edits the import statement in the source file
qa.why: The runner hoists module mock calls so the replacement is in place before the real module loads.

qa.q: What does the final line do?
qa.right: It restores the real Date.now after the spy
wrong: It deletes the spy's recorded calls but keeps returning 0
It makes Date.now return the current time permanently as 0
It mocks the whole Date object
qa.why: mockRestore removes the spy and puts the original method back.

qa.q: Why does this test pass without waiting a second?
qa.right: Fake timers let the test advance the clock by hand
wrong: The callback is called synchronously by setTimeout
vi.fn skips the delay of timers it wraps
The runner ignores timeouts under two seconds
qa.why: With fake timers, advanceTimersByTime fires the scheduled callback instantly.

qa.q: A service's unit tests mock every function, yet a wrong SQL query shipped. What change helps most?
qa.right: Add an integration test that runs the query against a real database
wrong: Mock the query builder as well
Raise the coverage threshold to 100 percent
Convert the tests to snapshot tests
qa.why: Mocks cannot prove that the real query is correct; a real database can.

qa.q: What is the second argument to toMatchSnapshot for?
qa.right: Property matchers that let the id and date match by type instead of exact value
wrong: A custom file name for the snapshot
A timeout for the comparison
A flag that updates the snapshot
qa.why: Non-deterministic fields would otherwise fail the snapshot on every run.

qa.q: After an intended UI change, many snapshot tests fail. A developer runs the update flag across the whole suite and commits. What should have happened first?
qa.right: Review each snapshot diff to confirm every change was intended, then update
wrong: Delete the snapshot files and commit without them
Disable snapshot tests until the redesign ends
Raise the pixel tolerance
qa.why: Blind updates turn snapshots into rubber stamps that approve defects.

qa.q: Why do CI pipelines often run jest with --ci?
qa.right: It stops new snapshots being written automatically, so a missing one fails
wrong: It makes tests run in a browser
It deletes obsolete snapshots
It disables coverage collection
qa.why: In CI an unexpected missing snapshot should be an error rather than a silent new file.

qa.q: What happens with this configuration?
qa.right: The run fails when line coverage is below 80 percent
wrong: Only files with 80 lines are counted
Tests are retried 80 times
Coverage is collected for 80 percent of the files
qa.why: A threshold turns a coverage report into a gate.

qa.q: A team has 95 percent line coverage and still ships a defect. Which technique tells you whether the tests would notice a changed condition?
qa.right: Mutation testing
wrong: Increasing the line coverage threshold
Running the suite in watch mode
Snapshot testing the whole module
qa.why: Coverage shows execution, not detection. Mutants that survive reveal weak assertions.

qa.q: Coverage reports 92 percent, but several source files are never imported by any test. What should the team do?
qa.right: Configure the coverage include pattern so all source files are counted
wrong: Lower the threshold to 80
Exclude those files with ignore comments
Switch to a different assertion library
qa.why: Files that no test loads can be left out of the percentage unless included explicitly.

qa.q: What does watch mode do?
qa.right: It reruns the relevant tests whenever you save a file
wrong: It runs the tests on the production server
It repeats the full suite forever without stopping
It records a video of the tests
qa.why: Watch mode gives fast feedback during development.

qa.q: How does test_health receive client?
qa.right: pytest matches the argument name to a fixture and injects its return value
wrong: It is imported at the top of the file
The test must call client() itself
It is a global variable set by pytest
qa.why: Fixtures are requested by naming them as parameters.

qa.q: How many test cases does pytest report for this test?
qa.right: Three, one for each tuple
wrong: One, because there is a single function
Six, one for each value
Zero, because parametrize needs a plugin
qa.why: Each parameter set becomes its own test case.

qa.q: Why call a factory with an override like this?
qa.right: The test shows only the field that matters, and defaults fill the rest
wrong: Factories require every field to be passed
It makes the test depend on database ids
It prevents the object from being valid
qa.why: Overrides keep the test's intent visible.

qa.q: Tests pass when run alone but fail intermittently in parallel against one shared database. What fix is most appropriate?
qa.right: Give each worker its own database or schema
wrong: Increase the test timeout
Turn on automatic retries
Add fixed sleeps between tests
qa.why: Parallel files overwrite each other's rows in a shared database.

qa.q: Tests run on in-memory SQLite while production uses Postgres, and a JSON query passes in tests but fails in production. What is the best response?
qa.right: Run the integration tests against a real Postgres, for example with Testcontainers or a service container
wrong: Add more unit tests with mocks
Rewrite the query to avoid JSON
Disable the failing test
qa.why: A different dialect hides engine-specific behaviour.

qa.q: What does this code do?
qa.right: It starts a disposable real Postgres container and returns its connection URL
wrong: It starts an in-memory SQLite database
It mocks the pg module
It restores a database backup
qa.why: Testcontainers creates throwaway services for integration tests.
qa.code:
const pg = await new PostgreSqlContainer().start();
const url = pg.getConnectionUri();

qa.q: What does this Playwright assertion check?
qa.right: That axe found no accessibility violations on the page
wrong: That the page loads in under a second
That every link on the page works
That the page has no JavaScript errors
qa.why: AxeBuilder runs axe-core on the live page and returns violations.
qa.code:
const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();
expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);

qa.q: A team says the site is accessible because the axe scan passes. What is the best response?
qa.right: Automated rules catch only part of the problems, so keyboard and screen reader checks are still needed
wrong: Axe passing proves WCAG conformance
Axe results are always false positives
Lighthouse must replace it
qa.why: Tools cannot judge things such as whether alt text is meaningful.

qa.q: What is toHaveNoViolations?
qa.right: A custom matcher from jest-axe that fails when axe reports violations
wrong: A built-in Jest matcher for DOM nodes
A Playwright method for screenshots
A Testing Library query
qa.why: jest-axe adds it to expect.

qa.q: What does this k6 threshold do?
qa.right: It marks the run failed if the 95th percentile request duration reaches 500 ms
wrong: It limits the test to 500 requests
It sends 95 requests per second
It stops the script after 500 ms
qa.why: Thresholds turn metrics into pass-or-fail criteria.

qa.q: A load test reports a good average latency but users complain of slowness. What should the team look at?
qa.right: Percentiles such as p95 and p99
wrong: The total number of virtual users
The size of the test script
Only the fastest request
qa.why: Averages hide the slow tail that individual users experience.

qa.q: A load tool waits for each response before sending the next request, and a server stall makes the report look fine. What is this measurement problem called?
qa.right: Coordinated omission
wrong: Think time inflation
Open model drift
Warm-up bias
qa.why: The tool omits the requests it would have sent during the stall, understating latency.

qa.q: What does wait_time = between(1, 3) represent in this Locust file?
qa.right: Think time, a pause of one to three seconds between tasks
wrong: The server's response time limit
The number of users added each second
The test duration
qa.why: It models a person pausing between actions.

qa.q: What does this command do on a CI machine?
qa.right: It runs the second of four slices of the suite
wrong: It runs four tests in parallel on two workers
It retries failures twice
It runs only the second test file
qa.why: Sharding splits files across jobs to cut wall-clock time.

qa.q: Visual tests pass locally but fail in CI with tiny text differences. What is the likely fix?
qa.right: Generate and compare baselines in the same container image used by CI
wrong: Raise the pixel tolerance to ignore all differences
Remove the screenshots
Use a smaller viewport
qa.why: Font rendering varies by operating system, so baselines should come from the same environment.

qa.q: A Playwright job fails in CI but never locally, and the runner is destroyed afterward. What helps debug it?
qa.right: Upload the trace and screenshots as artifacts on failure
wrong: Raise the retry count
Cache the dependencies
Remove the headless setting
qa.why: Artifacts preserve evidence that would otherwise vanish with the runner.

qa.q: A team sets CI retries to 3 and the dashboard stays green. What should they add?
qa.right: Report tests that pass only on retry as flaky and track them for fixing
wrong: Raise retries to 10
Delete tests that failed once
Disable the retry setting but ignore failures
qa.why: Retries hide instability unless passed-on-retry tests are surfaced.

qa.q: A committed test.only makes CI run a single test and pass. Which setting prevents this?
qa.right: A forbid-only setting that fails the run when a focused test exists
wrong: Setting a longer timeout
Enabling watch mode
Running tests in a random order
qa.why: Focused tests silently disable the rest of the file.

qa.q: A test passes alone but fails after another test in the full run. The mock is declared at module level and never cleared. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Clear or restore mocks after each test, for example in afterEach or through config
wrong: Run only that test in CI
Put a sleep before the failing test
Make the mock return different values
qa.why: Shared mock state leaks calls and implementations between tests.

qa.q: A provider team renames a response field. Which test is designed to catch this before deployment?
qa.right: The provider's verification of the consumer's contract
wrong: The consumer's unit tests
A snapshot of the API client
A load test of the endpoint
qa.why: Consumer-driven contract tests record expectations that the provider verifies.

qa.q: A mutation testing report shows a surviving mutant. What does that mean?
qa.right: No test failed when the code was changed, so the tests have a gap
wrong: The code was changed incorrectly
Coverage was below the threshold
The test suite ran too slowly
qa.why: A surviving mutant shows that behaviour is not asserted.

qa.q: Why create the cart in beforeEach rather than as a shared constant at the top?
qa.right: Each test gets fresh state, so tests do not depend on order
wrong: beforeEach runs faster than a constant
A constant cannot hold objects
It lets tests share the same cart on purpose
qa.why: Fresh state per test removes order dependence.

qa.q: What does this Mock Service Worker handler do?
qa.right: It answers GET /api/user with JSON for any code making that request, without changing app code
wrong: It edits the app's fetch calls at build time
It starts a real API server on a port
It records requests and sends them to a vendor
qa.why: MSW intercepts at the network layer.

qa.q: A ggsocial test fails because an imported module pulls in the server-only package. What does ggsocial's Vitest setup do about this?
qa.right: It aliases server-only to a stub in the config
wrong: It switches the tests to a browser environment
It removes the import with a Babel plugin
It installs a different Next.js version
qa.why: The package deliberately throws outside a real Next.js server build, so the config aliases it to a stub.

qa.q: How can ggmoney check that its tests behave identically on MySQL, which runs in strict mode?
qa.right: Set GGMONEY_TEST_DRIVER=mysql and the DB_* variables to run the same assertions on MySQL
wrong: Rewrite the tests as Jest tests
Run them only against SQLite
Use PHPUnit for the MySQL run
qa.why: By default the suite uses SQLite. The variable runs the same checks against MySQL.

qa.q: Why do Moksy's *.itest.mjs suites use a real Mongo instead of a mock?
qa.right: Unique indexes and guarded updates cannot be proven with a mock
wrong: Mocks are not supported by Vitest
Mongo is faster than a mock
The CI workflow has no mocks
qa.why: Only a real database enforces index and update behaviour. CI starts a Mongo service container.

qa.q: A reviewer says Moksy has Playwright browser tests because Playwright is in a package.json. What is the best response?
qa.right: It is only a declared dependency in one package and no playwright config exists, so browser e2e is not established
wrong: Moksy runs Playwright in ci.yml
Playwright tests are in the dashboard e2e script
Moksy replaced Playwright with Jest
qa.why: The dashboard e2e script runs a Vitest flow test instead of a real browser.

qa.q: How does ggsocial's makeTestDb avoid needing a live Postgres?
qa.right: It creates an in-memory Postgres with PGlite and builds the real schema with pushSchema
wrong: It mocks every query to return empty rows
It uses SQLite with a translated schema
It starts a Docker container per test
qa.why: The same dialect and schema keep tests fast and close to production.

qa.q: What does GGLearn's check:dynamic verify?
qa.right: That each stated answer of the dynamic question families matches what real execution produces
wrong: That login and scoring logic work
That every page renders in a browser
That the deploy script succeeds
qa.why: It runs real tools such as node, python and git to check answers. It does not cover application logic.

qa.q: Which of these is a valid reason to use Vitest in a Vite project?
qa.right: It reuses the same Vite configuration and transforms for tests
wrong: It is the only runner that supports TypeScript
It runs tests in a real browser by default
It needs no configuration at all for aliases in any project
qa.why: Sharing configuration with Vite is a main selling point of Vitest.

qa.q: Which protocol does Selenium WebDriver use to control browsers?
qa.right: The W3C WebDriver protocol
wrong: The Chrome DevTools Protocol only
GraphQL over HTTP
gRPC
qa.why: Selenium is built around the WebDriver standard.

qa.q: Why is a role-based locator generally preferred over a deep CSS selector in browser tests?
qa.right: It survives layout refactors and reflects what assistive technology exposes
wrong: It runs faster in every browser
It removes the need for assertions
It works without any accessible names
qa.why: Role and name rarely change in a purely visual refactor.

qa.q: A team's unit tests spend most of their time in jsdom setup. Which change addresses this with the least rewriting?
qa.right: Try a lighter DOM environment such as happy-dom for tests that do not need full fidelity
wrong: Replace all tests with Selenium
Remove the DOM from the tests entirely
Turn on snapshots for every component
qa.why: happy-dom favours speed over completeness, with the risk of missing browser behaviour.
